verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for about three days: "I think it was about three, it's been about three days now" and describes it as watery and large volume: "it's like basically I think it's diarrhoea... super watery... just pouring straight from my bum".

Frequency and character: "I feel like it's like almost every hour, when I'm awake" and "it's just super watery". No blood: when asked about blood, patient says "no I don't, I don't remember anything... nothing like that".

Location and quality: "It's kind of... it's like at the bottom" and clarifies midline: "it feels pretty, like in the middle, to me. Not on any side, left or right." Intermittent: "it comes and goes." Intensity: patient estimates "maybe is that like a six, or a seven?".

Nausea and vomiting: "yeah I definitely feel kind of nauseous... I've have vomited" and "whenever I have like milk... I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually, yeah one time I just like had some milk, and I just completely vomited it." Vomiting less frequent than diarrhea is confirmed: Doctor: "the vomiting is not as... prominent as the diarrhea. Is that right?" Patient: "Uh no, no it's not."

Patient reports feeling febrile without measurement: "I think I am pretty, I feel kind of really hot all the time. And uh I'm pretty sure I'm burning up... I haven't actually done any temperature reading".

Fluids and food: patient says of fluids, "it just feels like the, the fluids do go down. But it just feels like it's going straight through." Regarding food: "I had some lunch today... But again it just it just came, come out pretty loose."
Decreased urination: in response to waterworks question, patient says, "yeah a bit, I guess less frequently maybe. Um but yeah, it seems to be OK."

Past medical history: Patient says, "yeah I think, I think otherwise I'm fit and well... I can't think of any related medical history... no I I don't think so."

Work: "I work at um an office, um in Central London. Um it's uh, so I work in government." Effort to attend work: "It's been tricky. Going to work with all of this. Um I dislike um, taking time off work. I feel like I I just want to go, um when I can. So I I try and go."

On Fridays I have more um alcohol" and later, "not every week, but maybe I'll once or twice a month, that yeah, I'll go out with my friends and drink a lot." This matches occasional weekday beers and binge drinking 1–2 times per month.

Diagnosis and features: Doctor states, "I think your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis... a bit of a basic infection of your tummy." Symptoms present in transcript: watery diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea, occasional vomiting, contact with brother with similar illness, and subjective fever as detailed earlier.

Doctor recommends OTC ORS but does not prescribe or specify package instructions: "you can get things like Diarolyte... It's probably worth recommending that." When asked, "Do i need like a prescription for that?" Doctor replies, "no, you can just get that over the counter." No prescribing action or instructions are stated.

Diet advice: Doctor says, "clear fluids. You can use soft diet, things like soup, mash. And then gradually build up, um as much as your body can tolerate." There is no mention of avoiding dairy temporarily in the plan.

Paracetamol advice: Doctor states, "you can try just you know regular Paracetamol if you are feeling feverish" and later, "If you are having, if you've got a bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think Paracetamol is very sensible." This matches PRN use for fever or pain.
Alcohol: Doctor says, "Try and avoid alcohol if you can." There is no advice in the transcript about avoiding caffeine or holding off on smoking.

There is no explicit mention of returning for persistent fever, blood in stool, severe pain, or inability to keep fluids down.
